types.oie_definition: A topic or theme that is being discussed or represented.
types.embedding_query_text: Subject Matter: A topic or theme that is being discussed or represented. Also called topic, theme, content area.

chosen_type.label: SubjectMatter
chosen_type.definition: A topic or theme that is being discussed, represented, or studied.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate precisely captures the abstract concept of a topic or theme; 'Conversation' is too specific to the act of discussion, not the content.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Syllabus
candidates.comment: A learning resource that describes the material covered in a course, often broken into sections with time requirements. Also called course outline, curriculum, study plan, course description. Examples: a university course syllabus, a training program outline, a workshop curriculum.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

types.oie_definition: Facts, details, or knowledge pertaining to past events or periods.
types.embedding_query_text: Historical Information: Facts, details, or knowledge pertaining to past events or periods. Also called historical data, past knowledge, historical facts.

chosen_type.label: HistoricalInformation
chosen_type.definition: Facts, details, or knowledge pertaining to past events or periods.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate represents the abstract concept of 'historical information' itself; candidates are either document types or events, not the knowledge.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.oie_definition: The theory and development of computer systems able to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
types.embedding_query_text: Artificial Intelligence: The theory and development of computer systems able to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence. Also called AI technology, machine intelligence, cognitive computing.

chosen_type.label: ArtificialIntelligence
chosen_type.definition: The theory and development of computer systems able to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate represents the abstract field or concept of Artificial Intelligence; 'SoftwareApplication' is too concrete.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: ControlAction
candidates.comment: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

types.oie_definition: A Uniform Resource Locator, which is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it.
types.embedding_query_text: URL: A Uniform Resource Locator, which is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it. Also called web address, internet link, website address.

chosen_type.label: URL
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `URL` data type directly represents a Uniform Resource Locator, which perfectly matches the OIE type and the provided mention.

candidates.label: URL
candidates.comment: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".

candidates.label: BreadcrumbList
candidates.comment: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

candidates.label: WPFooter
candidates.comment: The bottom section of a web page, typically containing copyright information, contact details, and navigation links. Also called page footer, website footer, site bottom. Examples: the copyright notice at the bottom of a website, links to privacy policy and terms of service, social media icons in the footer.

types.oie_definition: A specific day, month, and year, or a general point in time.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day, month, and year, or a general point in time. Also called calendar date, day, point in time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.oie_definition: A written or recorded item from the past that provides information or evidence about historical events.

chosen_type.label: HistoricalDocument

candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. types.oie_definition: A method or algorithm used for encrypting and decrypting information, often involving a set of rules or symbols.
types.embedding_query_text: Cipher System: A method or algorithm used for encrypting and decrypting information, often involving a set of rules or symbols. Also called cryptographic system, code system, encryption method.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size systems used for different product categories. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, apparel sizing convention. Examples: 'US', 'UK', 'EU', 'EN-13402', 'Imperial'.

chosen_type.definition: A general category describing a kind of established organization or facility.

candidates.label: NonprofitType
candidates.comment: NonprofitType is an enumeration for various official non-profit organization types. Also called charity type, non-profit classification. Examples: 501(c)(3) (US), Registered Charity (UK), Gemeinnütziger Verein (Germany). Distinct from NLNonprofitType, which is specific to the Netherlands.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

types.oie_definition: A person who studies and writes about the past, and is regarded as an authority on it.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: Photograph
candidates.comment: A Photograph, as a CreativeWork, is an image captured using a camera. Also called photo, picture, image. Examples: a portrait photograph, a landscape photo, a news photograph. Distinct from Painting, which is created with paint.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. candidates.label: PresentationDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A PresentationDigitalDocument is a DigitalDocument file containing slides or used for a presentation. Also called slide deck, presentation file, slideshow. Examples: a Microsoft PowerPoint file, a Google Slides presentation, a Keynote document, a PDF of presentation slides.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

types.oie_definition: A collection of integrated software components designed to work together to perform a specific function.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication

candidates.label: OperatingSystem

candidates.label: SoftwareSourceCode

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform

candidates.label: MobileApplication

candidates.label: BookFormatType

candidates.label: RefundTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: RefundTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different kinds of product return refund types. Also called return refund category, reimbursement type. Examples: full refund, store credit, partial refund, exchange.

candidates.label: DataType

candidates.label: UpdateAction

candidates.label: WPHeader

candidates.label: WPAdBlock

candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: Thesis

candidates.label: Researcher

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: 3DModel
candidates.comment: A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. candidates.comment: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. candidates.label: Observation

candidates.label: Distance

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate directly represents a 'cognitive state' as a mental condition or state of mind.

candidates.label: ActionStatusType
candidates.comment: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.

candidates.label: IncentiveStatus
candidates.comment: IncentiveStatus is an enumeration describing the current status of an incentive, such as whether it is active or expired. Also called incentive state, benefit status, program condition. Examples: 'Active', 'Expired', 'Pending', 'Suspended'.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

types.oie_definition: A measure of the intricacy or difficulty of something.
types.embedding_query_text: Complexity Level: A measure of the intricacy or difficulty of something. Also called difficulty level, intricacy, sophistication.

chosen_type.label: ComplexityLevel
chosen_type.definition: A measure of the intricacy or difficulty of something.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate directly represents a 'complexity level' as a measure of intricacy or difficulty.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: Rating
candidates.comment: A Rating is an Intangible representing an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars. Also called score, grade, review rating. Examples: a 4-star movie rating, a product's 8/10 score, a customer satisfaction rating of 5 out of 5, a restaurant's health inspection grade.

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

types.oie_definition: A quantifiable measure used to assess the efficiency, effectiveness, or quality of a process or system.
types.embedding_query_text: Performance Metric: A quantifiable measure used to assess the efficiency, effectiveness, or quality of a process or system. Also called performance indicator, key metric, measurement standard.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: 'Scale' and 'speed' are quantifiable measures, which align with the definition of Schema.org `QuantitativeValue`.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

types.oie_definition: An object made or modified by human culture, typically recovered by archaeological excavation.
types.embedding_query_text: Archaeological Artifact: An object made or modified by human culture, typically recovered by archaeological excavation. Also called ancient artifact, archaeological find, historical object.

chosen_type.label: ArchaeologicalArtifact
chosen_type.definition: An object made or modified by human culture, typically recovered by archaeological excavation.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate directly represents an 'archaeological artifact' as a human-made object from the past.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: Sculpture
candidates.comment: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping or combining materials. Also called statue, carving, monument, artwork. Examples: Michelangelo's David, Rodin's The Thinker, a modern abstract metal sculpture, a clay bust.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

types.oie_definition: A piece of land surrounded by water.
types.embedding_query_text: Island: A piece of land surrounded by water. Also called isle, atoll, landmass.

chosen_type.label: Island
chosen_type.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate directly represents an 'island' as a specific type of landform.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

candidates.label: Pond
candidates.comment: A Pond is a BodyOfWater, typically a small, still body of fresh water. Also called pool, small lake. Examples: a garden pond, a village pond, a duck pond, a natural depression filled with water.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: Volcano
candidates.comment: A landform, typically a mountain, with a vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are ejected. Also called active volcano, dormant volcano, volcanic mountain. Examples: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Kilauea.

types.oie_definition: A challenging question or unresolved issue pertaining to past events or periods.
types.embedding_query_text: Historical Problem: A challenging question or unresolved issue pertaining to past events or periods. Also called historical enigma, past mystery, unresolved historical question.

chosen_type.label: Question
chosen_type.justification: A historical puzzle is a specific query or unresolved issue, which aligns with the definition of Schema.org `Question`.

candidates.label: Question
candidates.comment: A Question is a Comment representing a specific query, often from a user seeking answers online or compiled in an FAQ. Also called query, inquiry, problem. Examples: "How do I reset my password?", "What is the capital of France?", a user's forum post asking for help, an item in an FAQ list.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: ComicStory
candidates.comment: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

types.oie_definition: A set of circumstances in which one finds oneself; a state of affairs.
types.embedding_query_text: Situation: A set of circumstances in which one finds oneself; a state of affairs. Also called circumstance, state of affairs, condition.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: A situation or case describes a set of circumstances or a state of affairs, which can be broadly categorized as an `Event`.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: UpdateAction
candidates.comment: The act of managing or changing the state or content of an object. Also called modify, edit, revise. Examples: updating a software application, editing a document, changing a profile picture.

candidates.label: FindAction
candidates.comment: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.
